frontier.hypothesis: regs_someone_prefers[72] can be driven to include $a1 and $a2 at exactly 34 instructions, which seats the pointer in $a3 with zero instruction cost.
frontier.mechanism: find_reg pass 0 (global.c:996-1001) excludes hard_reg_conflicts | ~regs_used_so_far | regs_someone_prefers; regs_used_so_far already contains every call-clobbered reg (global.c:365-367), so with the measured conflicts {2,3,4,29} a someone_prefers of {5,6} makes the first free bit 7 = $a3. Preferences emit no instructions. The bit pattern is not hypothetical: func_80027438 in the same TU shows someone_prefers {5,6} in this session's dump. Bottleneck is origination: prune_preferences (global.c:881-931) fills the set only from allocnos that conflict with 72 AND sit lower in allocno_order, and set_preference (global.c:1671-1716) can only name $a1/$a2 if they appear as literal hard regs in pre-RA RTL (this function has no calls and one param) or as a local-alloc seat.
frontier.next_probe: Instrument the origination side instead of guessing spellings: dump every single_set in the pre-RA RTL (the .greg/.lreg stage) for the baseline and check the claim that the offset-0 load is the ONLY SET whose src's first operand is a re-seatable pseudo. If a second one exists, that is the carrier; re-point it and re-read BB2_FINDREG_DEBUG=72 for someone_prefers. Reject on the dump, not the sandbox score.

frontier.hypothesis: A local-alloc quantity can occupy $a2 across the pointer's live range while emitting nothing, via local-alloc.c combine_regs coalescing plus final.c no-op-move deletion.
frontier.mechanism: The target needs an occupant at $a2 that emits no instruction. cross_jump (jump2) is the only post-local-alloc deletion channel the ledger examined and it is closed (s12 at both real branch sites; Judge FAIL 2026-07-21 for invented arms). Unexamined: local-alloc merges copy-related pseudos into ONE quantity, after which the connecting copy is reg-to-same-reg and is deleted by final.c's no-op move deletion (the same final.c:1800 path s6 cited) - the merged quantity still holds its hard reg across the union of both live ranges.
frontier.next_probe: Write a plain assignment between two real locals (ordinary C, no FAKE family needed if the value is real), confirm in the .lreg dump that combine_regs put both pseudos in one quantity, confirm in the objdump that the move is gone, then read BB2_FINDREG_DEBUG=72 to see whether the quantity's seat entered hard_reg_conflicts[72]. Measure insn count first: the probe is only interesting at 34.

frontier.hypothesis: A rederived shape that SUBSTITUTES an existing instruction (rather than adding one) can occupy a fifth register at 34 instructions.
frontier.mechanism: s11's 1:1 correspondence shows all 34 target slots are spoken for and 30 are already byte-identical, so any added occupant must replace an existing insn with one that both does that insn's job and holds an extra register. s14 supplies the acceptance test as a one-compile dump read rather than a sandbox cycle.
frontier.next_probe: Acceptance test BEFORE building: the shape must emit exactly 34 instructions AND show, under BB2_FINDREG_DEBUG on the pointer's pseudo, either conflicts superset-of {2,3,4,5,6} or someone_prefers superset-of {5,6}. Anything that adds a 35th slot is rejected without a sandbox run.
